en: The Dyad on Association with the Taints (Āsavasampayuttaduka), and the Triad on the Visible (Sanidassanattika).

Dependent on a state that is not associated with the taints (*āsava*), non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state dissociated from the taints, visible, and impinging, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … one.
Dependent on a state dissociated from the taints, non-visible, and impinging, there arises a state dissociated from the taints, visible, and impinging, by way of root condition … one.
(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three; under predominance condition there are three … pe … [and so forth].
In the case of resultant [condition], one; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, three.

(In the root of "not associated with taints, not visible, and impinging," there are exactly three. In the case of root, three; in the case of predominance, three; ... pe ... in the case of mutuality, one; ... pe ... in the case of resultant, one; ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, three.
Dependent on a state that is not associated with taints, not visible, and non-impinging, [arises] a state dissociated from taints, not visible, and non-impinging.
A state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of root; one in the case of predominance …pe… one in the case of non-disappearance.
